summary.headline: Brainbees Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to ₹2,106 crore, but India multi-channel gross margin fell ~260 bps YoY, holding adjusted EBITDA margin at 4.24%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to ₹2,106 crore, with GMV up 12% to ₹2,807 crore and AUTC up 10% to 11.8 million. Consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 4.24% from 4.98%, and gross margin dropped to 36.5% from 38.5%, mainly from India multi-channel diapering competition and manufacturing cost pass-through lag. Management said diapering competition is easing and that the crude/rupee cost pass-through completes by end-Q2, but gave no firm timeline for margin recovery. Growth drivers cited were RocketBees (over 50% of online shipments), FC Qwik (125,000 shipments in June across 12 cities) and offline GMV growth of 15%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Revenue +18% YoY, best in seven quarters; GMV +12%, orders +12%, AUTC +10%. Non-diapering is ~85% of GMV; gross margin down ~260 bps YoY and EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY on diapering competition and manufacturing input costs. Remains PAT positive.

segments.name: International (Middle East)
segments.commentary: Revenue +12% YoY, AUTC +7%, GMV +9%. Adjusted EBITDA loss reduced 22% YoY; loss-to-revenue improved from 10% to 7%. Management targets EBITDA neutrality but gave no timeline.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly flat due to a planned warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand, expected to complete in Q2 with growth recovering from Q3. Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% from 1%.

segments.name: Preschool (FirstCry Intellitots)
segments.commentary: Revenue +47% to ₹19 crore and adjusted EBITDA +65% to ₹5 crore. Over 500 preschools; management targets at least 1,000 over the next couple of years, organically, with no M&A being evaluated.

guidance_outlook: Management expects India multi-channel growth to stay elevated for subsequent FY27 quarters, citing RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline store expansion.
Crude/rupee-linked price increases in manufacturing expected to be fully passed on by end-Q2 FY27, with full margin normalisation for that component from Q3.
Diapering margin recovery expected over four to six quarters, with competitive intensity easing in July and August per management.
Adding around 100 net offline stores in FY27 (management said 90-100); FY28 expansion expected to be larger.
Management declined to give a timeline for International EBITDA breakeven, pointing to input metrics instead.
Management said the 280 bps gross margin gap should 'dramatically' reduce, but gave no quantified target for the full year.
capex_capacity: Offline store expansion was paused for two quarters to realign the product portfolio; now resuming with ~100 net new stores targeted in FY27.
RocketBees expanded from 62 to 72 cities and now handles over 50% of online shipments, a target set two quarters ago and met by June 2026. Delivery turnaround time improved ~20%.
FC Qwik (2-hour quick delivery) grew from ~60,000 shipments in five cities in March to 125,000 in 12 cities in June. Management targets 10% of total shipments on FC Qwik and 20% in specific pincodes.
Manufacturing business is passing crude-linked raw material and rupee-depreciation cost increases to customers.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces heightened competition from quick commerce discounting and new entrants. Management says branded diapering has started improving in Q1 and competitive intensity is softer in July and August.
Non-diapering categories (~85% of GMV, fashion >50% of GMV, home brands >50% of business) are performing well; management said gross margin is expected to improve through home brand and fashion mix.
GMV growth (12%) trails India revenue growth (18%) because the revenue line includes manufacturing and the GMV is at MRP, with GST 2.0 reducing MRP from Q2.
Management said non-diapering consumables are about 15% of India GMV, with healthy margins and no challenge from quick commerce.
Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 after the width-to-depth assortment change, which added lower price points without a material gross margin impact.

financial_highlights.value: Down ~260 bps YoY (~20 bps recovered vs Q4's 280 bps drop)

financial_highlights.metric: International adjusted EBITDA loss as % of revenue
GlobalBees adjusted EBITDA margin (post corporate expenses)

qa_highlights.question: Jay Laddha asked how much of the manufacturing-related gross margin loss was recovered in Q1 and whether International breakeven timing or FY27 guidance had any update.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India multi-channel gross margin recovered about 20 bps of the 280 bps Q4 drop, with full pass-through of crude and rupee costs by end-Q2. On International, Abhinav Sharma declined to give a breakeven quarter, pointing to inputs (home brand mix, high-margin brand curation, quality customer acquisition); the loss-to-revenue ratio moved from -16% in March 2025 to -7% in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Kumar asked whether India multi-channel growth can be sustained next quarter and when margin will recover.
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to remain elevated for the next few quarters on RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline stores. Margin recovery is expected faster than the 4-6 quarter diapering normalisation, with diapering competition easing in July and August and crude/rupee pass-through complete by end-Q2, full recovery likely from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Ranodeep Sen asked about the company's right to win in diapering against pharmacy and private-label entrants, and whether M&A is being considered in preschool.
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goel said diapering retention is hard for private labels and that quick commerce discounting is temporary; branded diapering showed some improvement in Q1. Supam Maheshwari said FC Qwik and the full-destination model support retention. On preschool, he said organic growth to at least 1,000 preschools over a couple of years, with no M&A being looked at yet.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked whether the sequential India multi-channel EBITDA margin decline is due to crude-linked inflation and whether H2 EBITDA margin will at least match last year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 280 bps Q4 drop had two components: diapering competition (expected to take 4-6 quarters to normalise) and manufacturing input costs (full recovery by end-Q2, normalised from Q3). Gautam Sharma bridged the 290 bps YoY India EBITDA margin decline as 260 bps gross margin loss plus 30 bps from logistics costs, partly offset by marketing and fixed-cost leverage. Supam Maheshwari said the 280 bps gap should 'dramatically' reduce, without a quantified target.

qa_highlights.question: Percy Panthaki asked why India revenue growth (18%) exceeds GMV growth (12%).
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the revenue line combines online, offline and manufacturing, while GMV is at MRP. GST 2.0, effective Q2, reduced MRP and contributed to the gap.

qa_highlights.question: Harsh Gokal Gandhi asked for the profitability delta between diapering and non-diapering and the company's share of the diapering category.
qa_highlights.answer: Supam Maheshwari said the delta between diapering and non-diapering has widened, with over 50% of GMV in fashion and over 50% of business in home brands. He said the delta should shrink as diapering margins recover; no market share figure was given. Archana Menon asked about store expansion and non-diapering consumables; management said about 100 net new stores in FY27 (90-100 per Gautam Sharma, net of attrition) and that non-diapering consumables are about 15% of GMV with healthy margins.

risks_watch: India multi-channel gross margin recovery: only ~20 bps of the 280 bps Q4 drop recovered in Q1; management expects full manufacturing pass-through by end-Q2 and diapering normalisation over 4-6 quarters.
Diapering competition from quick commerce discounting and new entrants (Apollo, MedPlus private labels) remains heavy; management says it is easing in July and August but gave no numbers.
International EBITDA breakeven has no timeline; management is pointing to input metrics. Middle East geopolitical disruption is a stated backdrop.
GlobalBees revenue flat on a warehouse and inventory transition for one core brand; management expects Q2 completion and growth from Q3, which is unverified until Q3 results.
Offline store expansion of ~100 net stores in FY27 after a two-quarter pause; capital efficiency and store productivity will need to be tracked.
Preschool scale-up target of at least 1,000 preschools over a couple of years; current base is over 500.
key_quotes: Overall business has grown 13% year on year. This is the strongest revenue growth in the last five years, that we have demonstrated on a consolidated basis
So we'll recover back this to 280, 20 is recovered to 260 will recover back, and then we'll grow back where we had wanted to reach.
The 280 bps will further dramatically should reduce.This is what we will say. Yes.
So, fairly confident that the category itself will optimize over the next couple of quarters.
I won't be able to comment on the M&A, it's too early. I don't think we are looking at it yet.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and on diapering and manufacturing margin recovery, but cautious on timing: it declined to give a International EBITDA breakeven date and gave no quantified full-year gross margin target. Answers often pointed to input metrics and qualitative drivers rather than numbers.

Preschools: not less than 1,000 over next couple of years (currently over 500)
